opener: Lord, I keep describing the bones instead of speaking to them.
paragraphs: I can give You a full report on what's dead — the marriage that's gone quiet, the dream I buried under a hundred disappointments, the body that doesn't answer the way it used to. I know every bone in this valley by name, Father, because I've walked it so many times. But I've noticed I stopped praying over it a while back. I just started narrating it instead, like a tour guide pointing at ruins, as if describing the damage carefully was the same thing as believing You could still do something with it.

Forgive me for the difference between grieving what's dry and giving up on it. Teach me to do what Ezekiel did — stand in the middle of what looks finished and speak to it anyway, not because I can see the breath coming, but because You told me to open my mouth before I see anything move. So I speak to it now: whatever in me is dry, hear the word of the Lord. You are not too far gone for breath to find You. In Jesus' name, amen.
